content_sections.heading: Hassan District Court Peon Selection Procedure
content_sections.text: Recruitment follows the Karnataka Civil Services (General Recruitment) Rules and the Karnataka Subordinate Courts (Clerk and other posts) (Recruitment) Rules 1982, as amended in 2007 and 2021. There is no written examination. Candidates are called for an interview based on the marks obtained in their SSLC examination, in the ratio of 1:10 against the number of vacancies notified for each post/category (i.e., 10 candidates called per vacancy, ranked by SSLC marks). The interview assesses the candidate's efficiency and general knowledge, and carries 10 marks. Final selection is based on a combination of SSLC marks and interview performance, per the applicable recruitment rules. Selected candidates undergo a probation period of 2 years as per the Karnataka Civil Services (Probation Rules) 1977. During this period, candidates must pass the departmental examinations prescribed for the post, as well as a Kannada language examination.

content_sections.heading: How to Apply for Hassan District Court Peon Recruitment 2026
content_sections.text: Visit the Hassan District Court website: hassan.dcourts.gov.in/Judges/online-recruitment . Applications can be submitted online only, from 19 August 2026 to 17 September 2026, 11:59 PM. Read all instructions on the application form carefully before filling; applications with incorrect or incomplete information will be rejected. Enter your active mobile number and e-mail ID carefully – the court is not responsible for non-delivery of SMS/e-mail due to incorrect details. Upload a scanned colour photograph: 5 cm height x 3.6 cm width, maximum 50 KB, JPG format, with a white background – scan the physical photo directly (do not edit/paste the photo digitally). Upload a scanned signature in black ballpoint pen on white paper: 2.5 cm height x 7.5 cm width, maximum 25 KB, JPG format. Fill in all details completely, then pay the prescribed fee (where applicable) online. Download and retain a copy of the submitted application and the fee receipt; keep them safely until the recruitment process concludes, and bring them to the eligibility test/interview. Important: Applications must be submitted well before the closing date to avoid last-minute failure. Fee payment must be completed by 19 September 2026, within State Bank of India office hours. Once fee is paid, it will not be refunded under any circumstances.

content_sections.heading: Documents Required (Category-wise)
content_sections.text: SC/ST candidates: caste certificate in Form 'D' Category-1 candidates: caste certificate in Form 'E' Category 2A/2B/3A/3B candidates: caste and income certificate in Form 'F', from the concerned Tahsildar Rural reservation: certificate in Form-2 from the concerned Education Officer, per Government Order No. SiAsu/53/SeNeNi/2007 dated 04-01-2008 (General-category rural candidates must also submit a Creamy Layer certificate in Form-1 alongside Form-2) Kannada Medium reservation: certificate as per Government Order No. SiAsu 71 SeNeNi 2001 dated 24-10-2002, confirming study in Kannada medium from Class 1 to Class 10 Physically Handicapped reservation: medical certificate from a district-level medical board, per the format in Government Order No. SiAsu/115/SeNeNi/2005 dated 19-11-2005 Project-Displaced reservation: certificate from the concerned Tahsildar, per Government Order No. SiAsu/44/SeNeNi/2001 dated 27-07-2001 Ex-Servicemen: discharge/release certificate from military service Widows, bonded-labour-freed persons, and other age-relaxation claimants: certificate from the competent authority "Other" (third gender) category: certificate from the competent authority, per Section 6 of The Transgender Persons (Protection of Rights) Act, 2019 Educational certificates (SSLC or equivalent), all mark sheets/semester certificates, and degree/certificate confirming the position claimed Note: Reservation certificates claimed must be valid as on the closing date of application. Original documents must be produced for verification when called. If information filed by an applicant is found incorrect at the time of verification, the candidature will be rejected, and the applicant may also be liable for criminal prosecution for providing false information.

content_sections.heading: Important Conditions
content_sections.text: Applicants must be Indian citizens. Where reservation categories have no eligible/available candidates, those posts will be filled from other reservation-category candidates; if SC/ST posts remain unfilled even then, they will be filled from General category candidates as per applicable rules. Candidates called for the eligibility test/interview must appear at their own expense; no travel allowance is payable. Selected candidates will be governed by the New Pension Scheme (NPS) or the pension scheme notified by the Government, as applicable. The notified vacancies are subject to change. Already-employed government servants selected for this post must submit a "No-Objection Certificate" from their current employer within 30 days of publication of the select list. The Court does not correspond with candidates on any matter; address changes must be communicated in writing. A candidate found to be an impersonator, to have submitted forged/fabricated or falsified documents, to have suppressed material facts, or to have adopted any unfair means in the recruitment process or in connection with the appointment, is liable to have their candidature/appointment cancelled at any stage — from the interview stage or after appointment — besides being subject to criminal and legal proceedings, without prior notice.

faq.question: Q1. How many Peon posts are available at Hassan District Court?
faq.answer: A total of 48 Group-D/Class-IV Peon (Sevaka) posts across General, SC, ST, and other reservation categories.

faq.question: Q2. What is the last date to apply?
faq.answer: Online applications close on 17 September 2026 at 11:59 PM; fee payment must be completed by 19 September 2026.

faq.question: Q3. What is the educational qualification required?
faq.answer: A pass in SSLC (10th Standard) or an equivalent examination, with the ability to read and write Kannada.

faq.question: Q4. Is there a written exam?
faq.answer: No. Candidates are shortlisted for interview based on SSLC marks (1:10 ratio against vacancies), and final selection combines SSLC marks with a 10-mark interview.

faq.question: Q5. What is the age limit?
faq.answer: Minimum 18 years; maximum age (including the one-time relaxation applied to this notification) is 40 years for General, 43 years for Category 2A/2B/3A/3B, and 45 years for SC/ST/Category-1.

faq.question: Q6. What is the application fee?
faq.answer: ₹200 for General and most reserved categories; SC/ST/Category-1/PH candidates are exempted.

faq.question: Q7. Is this recruitment final?
faq.answer: It is subject to the outcome of Writ Petition Nos. 200448/2025, 17968/2025 & 3145/2023, currently pending before the Karnataka High Court.
